frames.does: What the played move itself does, visible on the board right after it.
frames.threatens: What the played move sets up for the mover's NEXT move, if the opponent does nothing about it.
frames.allows: What the played move lets the opponent do: read from the engine's reply line.
frames.better: What the engine's better move would have done: read from the engine's line from the position before the move. Only for moves that were not the engine's.

objects.piece: a role (pawn, knight, bishop, rook, queen, king) and its square, e.g. "knight c3"

concepts.definition: The move mates, lets the opponent force mate, or the better move forced mate.
A mate delivered on the king's own back rank, blocked in by its own pawns.
concepts.sentence: That mates on the back rank.

concepts.definition: The mover threatens mate next move (threatens), or the move lets the opponent threaten a mate that must be answered (allows).

detector.where: eval mateIn only; no null-move threat check

concepts.definition: A check with no bigger point that another concept covers.
concepts.sentence: A check, forcing the king to respond.

concepts.definition: The move leaves one of the mover's own pieces or pawns en prise: it can be taken for free or for less than it is worth.
Takes an enemy piece or pawn that was undefended or not defended enough, winning it outright.

detector.where: exchange.dart staticExchange > 0 on the captured square

concepts.definition: A sequence of trades that ends with material won; no named tactic is the reason.
concepts.sentence: That wins material once the trades are over.

concepts.definition: A plain capture that starts an exchange, when nothing more specific applies.
Takes back material the opponent just captured.
Offers or starts an even exchange of like pieces.
Trades pieces while ahead in material, heading for a simpler won ending.
concepts.sentence: Trading pieces when ahead is the way to convert.

concepts.definition: Gives up material on purpose for an attack or a larger gain.
An opening pawn offer for development or central control.
concepts.sentence: That offers a pawn for the centre.

concepts.definition: One piece attacks two or more enemy targets at once so one of them is lost.
concepts.sentence: That forks the {piece} and another piece.

concepts.definition: A piece cannot move (or should not) because a more valuable piece or the king stands behind it on the line.
Wins material because the piece that should defend (or recapture) is pinned.
concepts.sentence: That wins the {piece} because its defender is pinned.

concepts.definition: Attacks a valuable piece that must move, exposing a piece behind it on the same line.
Moving one piece opens a line for another piece behind it, which now attacks a target.
concepts.sentence: That uncovers an attack on the {piece}.

concepts.definition: A discovered attack whose target is the king.
A piece has no safe square to go to, so it can be won.
Attacks a piece that has no safe square to escape to.

detector.where: move_tags.dart _isTrapped exists; not tied to the attacking move

concepts.definition: Captures or deflects the piece that was defending a target, so the target falls.
concepts.sentence: That removes the defender of the {piece}.

concepts.definition: Adds another attacker to an enemy piece or pawn that is already attacked.
concepts.sentence: That adds another attacker on the {piece}.

concepts.definition: Attacks an enemy piece that is not adequately defended, threatening to win it.
A pawn attacks an enemy piece, which has to move.
concepts.sentence: The pawn attacks the {piece}, which has to move.

concepts.definition: A developing or improving move that also attacks something, so the opponent loses time answering it.
concepts.sentence: That gains a tempo on the {piece}.

concepts.definition: Moves an attacked piece to a safe square.
Defends a piece or pawn that was hanging.
Captures, blocks or drives off the piece that was attacking one of the mover's pieces.
concepts.sentence: That attacker is gone; the {piece} is safe.

concepts.definition: Parries a concrete threat (mate, fork, winning material) the opponent had.

A piece already en prise is left there. ALLOWS when that is the mistake; DOES / BETTER when it is the engine's own move and the threat is ignored on purpose ("Ignoring the threat on the queen, a difficult move to see").
concepts.sentence: That ignores the threat to the {piece}.

concepts.definition: Castles, tucking the king away and connecting the rooks.
Clears the last piece between king and rook so castling becomes possible.
concepts.sentence: That clears the way to castle {side}.

concepts.definition: A pawn move in front of the castled king that gives it an escape square against back-rank mates.
concepts.sentence: That gives the king some air.

concepts.definition: Weakens the pawns or pieces sheltering the mover's own king, or gives up castling, and the engine line attacks it.
Brings the king toward the centre or the action in an endgame.
concepts.sentence: In the endgame the king is a fighting piece.

concepts.definition: Moves a knight or bishop off its starting square in the opening.
Occupies or supports the central squares (d4, d5, e4, e5).
Moves a piece to a square where it controls clearly more (mobility gain) without a tactical point.
concepts.sentence: That puts the {piece} on a more active square.

concepts.definition: Puts a rook on an open or half-open file.
concepts.sentence: That puts the rook on the open file.

concepts.definition: Puts a rook on the opponent's second rank (the seventh from the mover).
concepts.sentence: A rook on the seventh rank.

concepts.definition: A knight (or bishop) lands on a square in enemy territory that no enemy pawn can ever attack, supported by a pawn.
Retreats or places a piece where it does little, and the engine's better move was active.
Forces (does/better) or lets the opponent force (allows) two pawns of one side onto the same file.
Creates a pawn with no friendly pawn on either neighbouring file.
Creates, pushes or supports a pawn no enemy pawn can stop on its way to promotion.
A pawn strikes at the enemy's pawn chain (usually its base or a lever), to open lines.
Promotes a pawn, or the line forces one.
A book move; the opening's name is the comment.
The only move that keeps the position (Great).
The opponent had just blundered and this move lets the win go (Miss).
concepts.sentence: That lets the opponent's mistake go.

concepts.definition: No concrete concept: the line only praises or criticises the move, or states the swing ("your advantage is gone").
The king steps out of check (to a square where it is safe), when that is the whole point of the move.
concepts.sentence: The king steps out of check.

detector.where: the position before is in check (dartchess isCheck)

concepts.definition: In a king-and-pawn ending, the king takes the opposition: it faces the enemy king with one square between them and the other side to move.
Stops an enemy passed pawn: blockades the square in front of it, controls its path, or captures it.
Leaves (allows) or creates (does/better) a pawn that has fallen behind its neighbours and can no longer be defended by a pawn.
Builds a diagonal chain of pawns that defend each other.
The only legal move.
A move inside a forced mate sequence that keeps the mate on track, short of the mate itself.
concepts.sentence: Keeping the mating attack on track.

detector.where: eval mateIn on both sides of the move

concepts.definition: Checks the king again and again, so the game is drawn: the move starts a perpetual or keeps one going (does), lets the opponent force one (allows), or the better move forced one (better). The engine scores the position a draw and its line is checks only.
concepts.sentence: That forces a draw by perpetual check.

concepts.definition: Lines up a second rook (or a queen and a rook) on an open or half-open file, or clears the square so the next move in the engine line does.
concepts.sentence: That doubles the rooks on the {file}.

detector.where: board_concepts.dart _doubleRooks; detect_concepts.dart (prepares, from the reply line)

concepts.definition: The move leaves the opponent with no legal move and not in check: the game is drawn (does). The reply line ends in a stalemate the opponent forces (allows), or the better line forced one (better).

detector.where: dartchess isStalemate, on the board after the move and at the end of a line

concepts.definition: The move brings about the same position (pieces, side to move, castling, en passant) for the third time or more in the game: a draw by repetition.
concepts.sentence: That repeats the position for the third time: a draw by repetition.

detector.where: the game's positions before the move, keyed by FEN without counters

concepts.definition: The move leaves neither side enough material to mate (it was not so before): the game is drawn.
concepts.sentence: That leaves too little material to mate: the game is drawn.
